findings.summary: The shared validation/error contract needs an explicit unsupported-operation result and composition with #84's descriptor classifier.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/66/design.md:58-64 validates operation/flags but defines only Invalid, Io and Stopped, with Invalid -> EINVAL and every other result -> EIO; it then says unsupported mappings are frozen. Current ublk.rs:1279-1281 and :1454-1456 returns EOPNOTSUPP for unsupported operations, which none of those shared errors can represent. #84 design.md:43-63 explicitly selects one descriptor classifier used by both modes, with registration-first EIO, unsupported flags/operations EOPNOTSUPP, and invalid read/write ranges EINVAL. #66 currently mentions #84 only for flush/discard behavior (:88-90), so its proposed universal validation contract is incomplete at the precise error distinction S2 requires.
findings.fix: Specify the boundary between ublk descriptor classification and common Request validation, preserving a typed Unsupported/refusal result or an explicit adapter-level Refuse(errno) before common admission. Add a whoever-lands-second hook to move/reuse #84's sole classifier without a second conflicting descriptor decoder; carry its configured max_io and precedence into both modes. Extend the concrete table/transcript fixture to assert EOPNOTSUPP for unknown op/unsupported flag, EIO for registration-first failure, EINVAL for invalid range, and zero engine/staging work on refusal. No dependency plan needs changing.

findings.summary: Fresh request bindings must be explicitly separate from the preserved device lifetime and the endpoint states used by #48.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/66/design.md:29-32 gives a registry entry a current-process Binding and Endpoint::Ublk{id,dev_t,held_fd}; :46-47 requires a successor's fresh binding, but :155-158 leaves kept/device-less states to later reconciliation. #15 device-lifetime-contract.md requires the full (volume,first_epoch,boot_uuid,instance,generation,rdev,diskseq) identity in device-info and conditional detach. #48 design.md:289-312 requires that exact original device tuple survive recovery while routing separately uses a new generation; kept entries have no held fd. A new Binding cannot supply that original tuple, and the proposed held-fd endpoint shape does not represent a kept device. The plan promises unchanged typed status/control behavior without spelling out these two distinct identities or a representable kept state.
findings.fix: Add the concrete whoever-lands-second semantic composition now: immutable adapter/device lifetime metadata retaining the full #15 tuple independently of fresh routing Binding; kept/resuming/running endpoint states with held fd only when actually open; describe/device-info/conditional detach use the preserved tuple while all I/O routes use only the new binding. Preserve #17 maintenance entries without manufacturing a client frontend/endpoint or admitting client I/O. Exact Rust signatures can remain for the approved thin prototype. Name fixtures proving pre-restart conditional detach still matches after recovery, stale predecessor events cannot reach new requests, kept status requires no fabricated fd, and maintenance starts allocate no frontend.

findings.summary: The Open questions introduction still says the approved timing and test-only choices are unaccepted.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/66/spec.md:81-82 says neither 'after #15' nor 'test-only' is recorded as accepted here, immediately before :85-87 records both as settled; decisions.md:14-25 preserves their approval.
findings.fix: Label :81-83 as historical pre-approval questions or replace the stale present-tense introduction with the settled choices, retaining the original approval record and prototype settlement.
